challenges.name: sealed-switch-guards-dominance-quiz
challenges.title: Exhaustive switches, guards and case order
challenges.description: Predict what a switch with record patterns and guards returns, and which switch bodies over a sealed interface the compiler accepts.

questions.explanation: Cases are tried from top to bottom and the first one whose pattern matches and whose guard is true wins. Card("4242", 2_000_000): the first pattern matches and 2,000,000 > 1,000,000, so "review" (the "visa" case is never reached for it). Card("4242", 50_000): the first guard is false, so matching goes on; "4242" starts with "4", so "visa". Card("5555", 50_000): both guards are false, and the unguarded case Card c catches it: "card". The GiftCard is not a Card, so only case GiftCard g matches, whatever the amount: "gift". The switch compiles: it covers both permitted types, so no default is needed, and both guarded Card cases come before the unguarded one, so nothing is dominated. "visa visa card gift" would need the "4" guard to be checked first; "review review card review" would need the amount guard to apply to every type.

options.text: It does not compile: a switch over an interface needs a default case

questions.explanation: A compiles: it has one case for each permitted type, so the switch is exhaustive without default. B does not compile: EWallet is not covered, and javac reports "the switch expression does not cover all possible input values". C does not compile: case Card c already matches every Card, so the guarded Card case below it could never run; javac reports "this case label is dominated by a preceding case label". D compiles: the guarded case comes first and the unguarded case Card c catches the cards the guard rejects. E compiles: default covers BankTransfer and EWallet - but it also means the compiler will not warn you when a new type is added, which is exactly what a sealed type is for.

options.text: A:  case Card c -> 1;  case BankTransfer b -> 2;  case EWallet e -> 3;
B:  case Card c -> 1;  case BankTransfer b -> 2;
C:  case Card c -> 1;  case Card c when c.amount() > 1_000_000 -> 2;  case BankTransfer b -> 3;  case EWallet e -> 4;
D:  case Card c when c.amount() > 1_000_000 -> 2;  case Card c -> 1;  case BankTransfer b -> 3;  case EWallet e -> 4;

challenges.name: settlement-fee-calculator
challenges.title: Write fee(Payment p) with a sealed switch
challenges.description: The Mekong Books settlement report reads the day's payments, one per line ("CARD 4242 250000", "BANK VCB 1200000", "EWALLET MOMO 99000", "GIFT GC-001 50000"), and the runner turns each line into a record of the sealed interface Payment. Replace last year's instanceof chain with fee(Payment p): a switch with record patterns and when guards, no default. Cards pay 2% (at least 3,000), bank transfers 2,200 below 500,000, 5,500 up to 999,999 and nothing from 1,000,000, e-wallets 1.5% (ZaloPay 1%), gift cards nothing; everything rounded down with long arithmetic. The runner prints one line per payment and a TOTAL line; the exact rules are in the starter.
